card.name: Clause breaks in general web prose
card.fires_on: Punctuation such as commas and colons, and occasional words, at a clause break in non-medical web text. Typical spots: after a proverb's first half, after a title, or before a question heading.

modes.label: Comma after first clause
modes.description: A comma that closes the first half of a saying or sentence, just before 'and' or 'but'.
modes.example: You may lead the horse to water<<,>> but you can't make it drink.

modes.label: Colon after a title
modes.description: A colon between a book's main title and its subtitle.
modes.example: 1491<<:>> New Revelations of the Americas Before Columbus

modes.label: Question heading start
modes.description: The opening word of a question heading in a health article.
modes.example: All of these can cause CO to spread throughout a building. <<Why>> do I need this test?

card.writes: Weak effect: it slightly favors words like 'basics', 'representation' and 'explicit', and Chinese emphasis words such as '显然'.
card.plain: It marks a pause point in ordinary prose, mostly commas, where a second clause is about to start.
